results.content: Specifically, this study focuses on the following key issues: combining the research progress in the field of art therapy, outlining the research ecology in terms of the number of publications, major journals, core countries or regions, authors’ collaborative networks, and institutional distribution; secondly, analyzing the characteristics of the distribution of disciplines in the field, and analyzing the patterns of cooperation between disciplinary categories and the academic influence of highly cited papers; thirdly, mining the research hotspots and thirdly, the research hotspots and development trends of art therapy will be explored, and keyword co-occurrence analysis, cluster mining, and timeline projection will be used to reveal the evolution and future direction of the discipline, which will provide the basis for promoting the deepening of theories and expanding the practice of art therapy.

results.title: Creative data justice: a decolonial and indigenous ...
results.content: The decolonial framework is rooted in the indigenous systems of care (Silva et al., Citation2022) which entails: (1) reframing value systems by attending to a diversity of aesthetic standards and (geo)politics of creative value; (2) pluralizing evaluation criteria that values creative forms within their contextual milieu rather than relying on universalized and hierarchical frameworks; (3) promoting reciprocal knowledge exchanges between creative stakeholders from the Global North and South; (4) developing North–South networks to support the agency and solidarity among creators and institutions globally that are committed to democratic and fair creative value, and South–South networks for direct exchange without the mediation of the Global North; (5) prioritizing indigenous practices and narratives to sustain local cultures and resist homogenization, and build guardrails to prevent their creative value from being co-opted or commodified by global markets; (6) critical engagement with power dynamics by contextualizing creative works within their historical and contemporary geopolitical settings; (7) developing fair and equitable practices within the global creative economy that prioritize the interests of especially underrepresented creators from the Global South; and (8) moving beyond the neoliberal market-driven value by including alternative economic systems such as cooperative ownership of creative work, or community-supported art projects that reflect collective, rather than individual value.

results.title: Browse by session
results.content: * ESSI1 – Next-Generation Analytics for Scientific Discovery: Data Science, Machine Learning, AI Large language models (LLMs) and agentic workflows are rapidly transforming scientific research by enabling new capabilities in literature and data discovery, analysis, coding and insight generation. We invite submissions on novel scientific applications of LLMs and agentic workflows, methods that ensure integrity and reproducibility, safety mechanisms (e.g., guardrails, risk mitigation, alignment), responsible AI frameworks (including human-in-the-loop design, fairness, and ethics) and lessons learned from real-world deployments. This session welcomes contributions on applications of deep learning in the full spectrum of earth sciences, submitted abstracts are related but not limited to: -Reservoir characterization, -Remote sensing, -Mineral exploration, -Natural hazard forecasting, -Hydrology, and climate modeling. This session invites contributions that advance the use of XAI to improve trust, interpretability, and robustness in ML applications across weather and climate domains — not only to validate and constrain models, but also to enable scientific discovery and insight.
